newsitem.title: DJIBOUTI: Djibouti opposition leader dies in Paris.
newsitem.headline: Djibouti opposition leader dies in Paris.

text.p: Mohamed Djama Elabeh, 55, a former Djibouti minister and chairman of the opposition Party for Democratic Renewal (PRD), has died in Paris, political sources said on Wednesday.

He had been receiving treatment at the Val de Grace hospital for about a week, and died on Tuesday. The cause of death was not known, but the sources said he was thought to have been suffering from diabetes.
Elabeh held a variety of ministerial portfolios over 15 years before switching to the opposition in 1992.
He came second in the presidential election of 1993, winning 25 percent of the vote.
President Hassan Gouled Aptidon expressed his condolences and said Elabeh "took an active part in the building of the Djiboutian nation".
Elabeh was considered a moderate, francophile leader with a broad-based political agenda that cut across the ethnic and clan divide of Djibouti politics.
